verdictProvider: No subagent judged anything in this round; the tester's own session ran every check, so no provider or model needs naming.

implementerProof.how: The implementer's case was driven independently in the deploy's order. Main's build before the block index (1357b95c) wrote 3 closed issues with 5 open asks each. The head's migration 0121, boot repair and block-index loop then logged withdrawn=15, documents=6 owed_documents=0 live_ahead=0. dispatch://UP-1/spec#b-85a89d0c-… and #b-e169c632-… resolve. After rebuild-refs (blocks_owed=6), the next tick gives owed_documents=0 and the references still resolve. On the same seed, 4440fc7b logs owed_documents=6 live_ahead=6 and the reference answers 'No block'. The proof is verified, but it covers only a difference in ask attributes.

failures.criterion: Architect's edge for the fix: a closed issue whose live document also differs from its latest version in something other than an ask attribute, with the pre-close settlement failing as the close allows, must still be block-indexed, so owed_documents reaches 0 and its #b- references resolve
failures.evidence: Red test TestBlockIndexIndexesAClosedDocumentWithAnUnsettledEdit, commit 196f5a85 in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/block_index_test.go. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://… go test -count=1 -run TestBlockIndexIndexesAClosed ./internal/dispatch/docs/. It fails with 'tick = {Documents:0 LiveAhead:1 OwedDocuments:1}, want the closed document indexed and nothing owed'; the two existing closed-document tests pass. Real surface, case 1, on the head: a trigger refused the document's versions while Chromium typed a line (settle ERROR); the daemon's SetStatus closed ED-1, logging 'close an issue whose documents did not all settle first'; the trigger was then dropped and rebuild-refs ran (blocks_owed=1); the block index logged owed_documents=1 live_ahead=1 and stayed owed through 2 more ticks, because resume.go:50 skips closed issues; a reopen settled the document at version 3 and indexed it. Case 2, the deploy order: main's build 1357b95c closed ED-1 with the typed line unsettled; the head's deploy logged documents=0 owed_documents=1 live_ahead=1, and each of the 4 blocks answers 'No block <id> in dispatch://ED-1/spec' while the issue stays closed. Main b69f636f gives the same result for case 1, so the cause is #2210's skip of a live-ahead document together with the rule that a closed issue settles nothing. This change did not introduce it, but the fix covers only a difference in ask attributes.

proof.criterion: A closed issue's document that the close or the ask repair left live ahead only in ask attributes is block-indexed in the deploy's order and after rebuild-refs, and its #b- references resolve
proof.surface: dispatch:local with the head's Go server on a database written by main before the block index, plus the dispatch CLI
proof.command: old-seed.sh dep_h (main 1357b95c: seed UP 3 and close by alice, by an agent and by SetStatus); run-server.sh at the head on dep_h; dcli doc-read --issue UP-1 --blocks; dcli read --ref dispatch://UP-1/spec#b-<id>; dispatch-e2e rebuild-refs with DISPATCH_SERVER_URL; wait 35 s; check document_block_versions
proof.observed: The boot repair gave withdrawn=15. The block index logged documents=6 owed_documents=0 live_ahead=0. The question block and the heading resolve ('Changed in version: 4'). rebuild-refs gave blocks_owed=6 with 6 of 6 null; the next tick gave documents=6 owed_documents=0, and the references still resolve.
